reason: The cited evidence does not address local heterogeneities, annealing effects, or transition broadening in FeMnNiGeSi HEAs. E1 discusses a different material system and temperature range, while E2 and E3 provide only general background on MCE and HEA potential without supporting the specific mechanistic claims.
premises: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi HEAs contain local chemical/structural heterogeneities that concentrate exchange interactions.
Subcritical annealing reduces these heterogeneities and homogenizes exchange interaction strengths.
Homogenization broadens the magnetostructural transition and lowers nucleation barriers.
Broader transition and lower barriers increase the effective temperature span of entropy change and reduce hysteresis.
The effect is specific to low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
